resources.string: Eye and brow processing
When off, eyes and brows use the model output directly and the eye and brow settings have no effect. Eye tracking and the model keep running.
0 bypasses all eye and brow post-processing and temporal smoothing; the output is the model value limited to [0, 1].
Mouth and tongue processing
When off, mouth shapes and the tongue use the model output directly and the mouth and tongue settings have no effect. Face tracking keeps running.
0 bypasses all mouth post-processing and temporal smoothing; the output is the model value limited to [0, 1].
Eye smoothing
Follows closely; small jitter shows
Steadier, but movements trail a little
s: strength. 0% skips this layer, 100% uses the smoothed result fully.
Eye small-movement speed
Small eye movements are held back; steadier gaze
Small eye movements follow quickly, and shake more easily
k: adaptive sensitivity, dimensionless. α₀ = 1 − exp(−k·|x − y₋₁|).
Blink snapping
Show the openness the model gives
Snap to fully open or closed near the ends
s: strength.
Snap-open line
Only nearly open eyes snap open; slight squints show
Slightly drooping eyelids also snap open
θ_low: lower Blink threshold, action coefficient 0–1.
Snap-shut line
Shallower closing already snaps shut
Eyes must close further to snap shut
θ_high: upper Blink threshold, action coefficient 0–1, above θ_low.
Brow smoothing
Brows follow closely; small shakes show
Steadier; raising and lowering are slower
s₁: strength of the composite smoothing.
Brow speed
Slower and steadier
Faster
w: update weight; 24 Hz reference share α₀ = w²·(1 − q·m).
Hold brows during blinks
Brows keep moving during blinks and eye turns
Brows stop for the moment of a blink or eye turn
q: eye-movement suppression. With q = 100% and m = 1, α₀ = 0.
Extra brow steadying
Use less of it; brow raises follow faster
Use it fully; steadier but slower
s₂: share of the Kalman result.
Steadying speed
Brow raises steadier and slower
Brow raises faster; small shakes show more easily
Q: process noise variance, in squared action coefficient. The steady state depends only on Q/R.
Steadying resistance
Brow raises faster; small shakes show more easily
Brow raises steadier and slower
R: measurement noise variance, in squared action coefficient. A smaller Q/R lowers the steady-state gain.
Raise or frown, not both
Raised-and-frowning brows show as they are
The weaker of the two is pushed down
s: strength.
Strictness
Both stay when they are similar
Even a slightly weaker one goes to near 0
p: exponent, dimensionless.
Wide eyes lift brows
Brows stay put when the eyes widen
Brows rise when the eyes widen
s: strength.
Wide-eye lift amount
Even fully wide eyes lift the brows only a little
Wide eyes lift the brows more
g: BrowInnerUp added per unit of Wide, dimensionless. By default fully wide eyes add 0.5.
Wide-eye lift stops at
Stops adding once the brows lift slightly
Keeps adding when the brows are already high
θ: add only while BrowInnerUp is below this, action coefficient 0–1.
Closed eyes lower brows
Brows stay put when the eyes close
Brows drop when the eyes close
s: strength.
Blink frown amount
Closed eyes add only a little frown
Closed eyes add more frown
g: BrowDown added per unit of Blink, dimensionless. By default fully closed eyes add 0.5.
Blink frown stops at
Stops adding once the brows lower slightly
Keeps adding when the brows are already low
θ: add only while BrowDown is below this, action coefficient 0–1.
Outer brow follow
Brow tails move as the model gives them
Brow tails match the inner brows
s: strength.
Mouth smoothing
Follows closely; small jitter shows
Steadier but trails; at 0% the extra smoothing is off too
s: strength, governing both passes.
Mouth small-movement speed
Small mouth changes are held back and follow slower
Small changes follow quickly, and jitter more easily
k: adaptive sensitivity, dimensionless, shared by both passes.
Jaw and smile extra smoothing
Jaw and smiles follow as fast as other shapes
These shapes steadier, but clearly slower with lower peaks
s₂: weight of the second pass in the composite share.
Leftover removal
Leftover shapes at rest stay
Leftovers removed cleanly; very slight shapes shrink too
s: subtraction strength. At 0 learning continues for the lip closure addition.
Leftover learning speed
Removed after a while; brief small movements are unaffected
Removed quickly; held slight expressions may be removed too
w: 24 Hz reference learning weight. At 50% the time constant is about 60 ms.
Leftover range width
Only values near the centre count as leftover; 0 stops learning
A wider range counts as leftover; slight movements are removed more easily
h: half-width of the learning interval, action coefficient.
Leftover range centre (other shapes)
Range moves down; only smaller values count
Range moves up; larger values count too
c: centre of the learning interval for general channels, action coefficient.
Leftover range centre (jaw)
The jaw range moves down
The jaw range moves up; larger openings count too
c₅: centre of the learning interval for JawOpen (mouth33 index 5).
Largest removable leftover
Leftovers above this are not removed
Larger leftovers may be removed
L: subtract only while |β| < L, action coefficient.
Lip closure boost
Add nothing
Add the full amount from the settings below
s: strength.
Base boost
Adds less
Adds more, up to the limit
b: action coefficient.
Boost limit
Adds at most this much
Allows adding more
c: action coefficient.
Extra per leftover
Adds about the same whatever the leftover
The larger the leftover, the more it adds
a: multiplier of the β₇/d term, action coefficient.
Leftover step
A small leftover already adds more
More leftover is needed to add the same
d: divisor of β₇, action coefficient.
Shrink weak shapes
Mouth shapes keep the model\'s proportions
Weaker mouth shapes shrink more
s: strength.
Shrink and boost range
Little change between weak and strong
Weak shapes shrink more, the strongest is boosted more
k: log coefficient, dimensionless.
Keep weak shapes
The weakest shapes nearly vanish
Weak shapes keep more; strong ones are boosted more too
d: log offset, dimensionless.
Tongue smoothing
The tongue follows closely
Steadier; sticking out and pulling back trail
s: strength.
Tongue speed
Steadier; sticking out and pulling back are slower
Sticking out and pulling back are faster
w: 24 Hz reference weight. At 60% the time constant is about 45 ms.
Tongue trigger
No trigger; small tongue values show as they are
Below the line counts as no tongue; above it is boosted
s: strength.
Tongue trigger line
A slight tongue shows, with more false triggers
The tongue must come out further to show
θ: TongueOut threshold, action coefficient 0–1.
Boost past the line
Past the line the tongue comes out less
Past the line the tongue quickly comes out fully
g: dimensionless multiplier; the result is limited to 1.
